A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAM/CVR study and provide readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the appendix renumbering and table restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original VLM and human evaluations, captioning comparisons, LoRA fine-tuning results, and benchmark correlations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds VQAv2 evaluations, one-shot comparisons, 32B fine-tuning, human response times, and attention and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix A.9 introduces PC-I, a diagnostic adaptation that supplies ground-truth captions together with images, extending the text-only PC procedure. The principal SC, SC-I, PC, and supervised LoRA recipes otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual VQAv2 evaluation alongside the retained PAM, CVR, MMBench, and MMMU-Pro coverage (Table A.3.3). This extends external visual-question-answering coverage; the new PAM generation table documents existing tasks rather than introducing additional task types.

E2.justification: Table A.4.2 adds a One Shot comparator across all 22 task rows to the existing Base, SC, SC-I, and PC comparison. Appendix A.9 additionally compares PC against PC-I for attention allocation. Earlier model and captioning comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds several evaluation protocols: Qwen2.5-VL-32B fine-tuning with 1k and 100k trials, caption-token attention measurements under PC/PC-I, and runtime measurements over 10 trials per task on one A5000 GPU. Human response time also joins accuracy as an evaluation measure. These additions substantially expand the experimental settings without replacing the original evaluation design.

E4.justification: New analyses examine image-related attention dilution (A.9), self-captioning overhead (A.10), human task difficulty through response times (A.2), and dropout-related overfitting (Section 4.3.2). V2 also adds larger-model fine-tuning checks and PAM/CVR correlations with VQAv2 performance, substantially expanding diagnostic and generalization evidence.

E5.justification: V1 already reports mean accuracy with standard deviations. V2 adds significance stars with p < 0.05, 0.01, and 0.001 thresholds to Tables 2, 3, A.5.1–A.5.2, and A.6.1. The test procedure is unspecified, and the PDFs do not establish additional replicated runs or changed seed practices.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy values in Tables 1–3 and the MMBench/MMMU-Pro comparison are retained. Substantial new results include VQAv2 scores of 60.07% for 7B Base, 65.07% for SC, and 65.84% for LoRA 100k; one-shot results; mixed 32B fine-tuning outcomes; and human timing, attention, and runtime measurements. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over corresponding v1 scores.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The added attention analysis is empirical and introduces no substantive formal theory.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain cognitive profiling with PAM/CVR, identifying visual-reasoning bottlenecks, and demonstrating captioning and fine-tuning benefits. The abstract changes 'substantially' to 'moderately' and explicitly names VQAv2, but these refinements do not redefine the main contribution claims.

C2.justification: V2 newly acknowledges self-captioning's inference-cost limitation and discusses human response-time differences through a tentative training-data explanation. Section 4.3.1 shifts the proposed bottleneck from inadequate CoT prompting to inadequate CoT training, while A.9 develops the existing attention-capacity interpretation.

D1.justification: New Table A.4.4 documents PAM frame counts, distractor ranges, and operators; A.10 specifies timing hardware and trial counts. Section 4.3.2 explains dropout selection, while the final 0.2 setting was already documented in v1. Existing LoRA hyperparameters and prompt/code examples are retained, with the latter moved from A.7 to A.11.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds two visual-abductive-reasoning references and distinguishes hidden-cause inference from the paper's logical reasoning focus. Two multimodal in-context-learning references support the new one-shot discussion. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained. Local edits clarify dataset construction and revise explanatory wording; acknowledgments and additional appendix sections are added. Existing appendix material is renumbered without extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adds tables for human response times, VQAv2, PAM parameters, 32B fine-tuning, and runtime, plus VQAv2 correlation and attention plots. It splits the former joint captioning-validation table into separate model tables, expands A.4.2 with a One Shot column, and enlarges labels in existing correlation plots. This substantially expands and revises the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through VQAv2 and larger-model experiments, makes self-captioning costs explicit, and improves PAM reproducibility. These are useful gains over v1. Their impact is limited by unspecified significance tests, a still-tentative attention interpretation, and little discussion of the new 32B regressions, so the overall improvement is modest.
